in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my son, Alex. He's my only child.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know about Alex! I have a few questions to help determine your eligibility for Child Benefit.

First, could you tell me how old Alex is?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Since Alex is 17, his eligibility will depend on his current situation.

Is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, GCSEs, or equivalent) or on an approved training course?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he's not in college or anything right now. He actually left school recently, but he's just registered with the local careers service to figure out what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful to know.

When Alex registered with the local careers service, was this a government-approved training programme or body? Specifically, did he register with a careers service, Connexions, or a similar qualifying body that provides training or education guidance for young people?

Also, could you tell me when he left school and when he registered with this service?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it was the official careers service - you know, the one that helps young people figure out their next steps after leaving school. He left school just a few weeks ago, and he registered with them pretty much straight away after that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. It sounds like Alex has registered with an official careers service shortly after leaving school, which is relevant for Child Benefit purposes.

Just a couple more questions to confirm eligibility:

1. Are you responsible for Alex - meaning he lives with you, or you contribute at least the same amount as the Child Benefit rate towards his upkeep?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely - Alex lives here at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

One last question: Are you and Alex living in the United Kingdom (England, Scotland, Wales, or Northern Ireland)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, we live in the UK - we're in England.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Based on what you've told me, I have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me summarise the key points:
- Alex is 17 years old
- He recently left school and has registered with an official careers service
- He lives with you in England
- You are responsible for him

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

**For Alex:**
- He is 17 years old and living with you in England
- Although he has recently left school and is not currently in full-time education or training, he has registered with an official careers service shortly after leaving
- Under Child Benefit rules, a young person aged 16 or 17 who has left education can still qualify if they have registered with a qualifying body (such as a careers service) and are not in work for more than 24 hours a week

**Important things to note:**
- Child Benefit can continue in this situation for a limited period (up to 20 weeks from when he left education) while Alex is registered and deciding on his next steps
- If Alex starts a job working more than 24 hours a week, starts claiming certain benefits in his own right, or the extension period ends without him entering approved education or training, you would need to inform the Child Benefit Office as eligibility may change

I hope this helps! Is there anything else you'd like to know?
